clue.text: Good cast will accept a cut

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the word for cast holds the a

parts.note: a snake casts or sheds its skin

explanation.surface: A director's strong cast agrees to have a scene trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will accept' puts A inside SHED after G.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a deep cut or wound in the skin is a gash, so to be cut is to be gashed.

clue.text: Lawsuit covering university sale

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the lawsuit word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a legal action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A legal case about a university's sale of property.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a public sale where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: United shown in high definition, becoming polished

indicators.note: shown in places the united word inside the abbreviation

parts.note: united things are at one, one whole

explanation.surface: A football team broadcast in HD looks slicker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club; it means at one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a honed skill has been sharpened and refined, polished to a high standard.

clue.text: Disadvantages of support during ties

indicators.note: during means within, so the support word sits inside the ties word

parts.note: drawn games are ties
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Downsides of backing a team through drawn matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: drawbacks are snags or downsides, things counting against.

clue.text: Raised the sack, putting insect in

indicators.note: the insect is put in, so its word sits inside the word for the sack

parts.note: 'the sack' is slang for bed, as in 'hit the sack'
a roach is a cockroach, an insect

explanation.surface: Someone lifts up a bag and slips a bug inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like lifting the sack; it means brought up a subject. 'the sack' is slang for bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a topic is to raise it for discussion, so raised and broached share that sense.

clue.text: Spreads complete in case of banks

indicators.note: in places the word for complete inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: utter means complete, as in utter nonsense

explanation.surface: Everything spreads fully inside the banks of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes B and S from banks; 'in' puts UTTER between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Butters as a verb means spreads with a fatty layer, as on bread.

clue.text: Done time? That's clear

parts.note: something done is over, finished

explanation.surface: Someone finishes a prison sentence and is cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done time' suggests a prison term; it splits into done and time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: overt means open and plain to see, obvious, clear.

clue.text: Brewing ale cost us for this stew

indicators.note: brewing stirs things up, so the letters of ale cost us are rearranged

explanation.surface: Making beer cost us money to put into this casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: cassoulet is a French slow-cooked dish of beans and meat, a kind of stew.

clue.text: The quality of Messi at heart — hence lacking height

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, everything but the ends
lacking means missing, so the letter for height is removed from hence

explanation.surface: The footballer Messi's quality comes from within, so being short doesn't matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' takes ESS from Messi; 'lacking' drops H from HENCE, leaving ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its fundamental nature or quality.

clue.text: Will they keep the viewers in touch?

definitions.text: Will they keep the viewers in touch?

parts.words: Will they keep the viewers in touch?
parts.note: viewers are eyes, and these items sit in contact with, that is in touch with, the eyes

explanation.surface: Asks whether something will keep an audience informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' suggests a TV audience; here it means eyes, and 'in touch' points at contact with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: lenses worn directly on the eyeball are in physical contact with the eyes, the viewers.

clue.text: Authoritative book about poor dad being compliant

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the book's word goes round the rest

parts.note: a bible is any authoritative reference book

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of dad are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A reference book on a hard-up father who does as he's told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Authoritative book' is a bible in the sense of a standard reference; 'poor' scrambles the father's letters to DDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a biddable person is obedient and easily led, readily doing what is asked.

clue.text: Relocating North Yemen's capital is causing problems

indicators.note: relocating moves things around, so the letters of North are rearranged
a capital is the head or first letter of the word Yemen

explanation.surface: Moving northern Yemen's capital city is proving a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relocating' rearranges NORTH into THORN; 'capital' takes the Y of Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a thorny issue is a difficult, prickly one that creates trouble.

clue.text: Obstruction mainly by European nations originally acting as one unit

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letters of the two words are taken
mainly means most of, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a block is an obstruction

explanation.surface: European states mostly unite to obstruct, acting together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims BLOCK to BLOC; 'originally' gives EN from European nations.
explanation.definitionFit: French phrase used in English: en bloc means all together, as a single group.

clue.text: Feeling lazy — it's the garlic being cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests worked over, so the letters of the garlic are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone blames their sluggishness on garlic in the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lethargic means sluggish and lacking energy, feeling idle.

clue.text: Business needing to be more flexible about source of income

indicators.note: about means round, so the comparative wraps the single letter

parts.note: suppler is the comparative of supple, flexible

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: A company must bend more to protect where its money comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' takes the I of income, which 'about' puts inside SUPPLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplier is a firm that provides goods to others, so a business in that role.

clue.text: Punch admitted by goalkeeper for a team

indicators.note: admitted by means let in, so the word sits within the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper takes a punch for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like a goalkeeper punching the ball; here it means pierce.
explanation.definitionFit: To punch holes in something is to perforate it, piercing it through.

clue.text: Trials coming after prisoner disputes

indicators.note: coming after places the word for trials behind the word for prisoner

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
trials and tests are synonyms

explanation.surface: Court hearings follow once a convict files appeals.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: contests as a verb means challenges or argues against, as disputes does.

clue.text: Rude worker from France getting priority

indicators.note: getting priority means going first, so from and France come before the worker

parts.note: of can mean from, as in 'of noble birth'
F is the international code for France
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A French labourer is impolite when pushing to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting priority' puts OF and F ahead of HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an offhand manner is curt and casually impolite.

clue.text: Endorses merchandise that's less than perfect

definitions.meaning: to second a motion is to support or back it
flawed goods sold cheaply as imperfect

explanation.surface: Someone backs a sale of damaged goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Seconds are both supports for a proposal and slightly faulty goods sold off cheap.

clue.text: Continue to hold volunteers in check

indicators.note: in places the volunteers' letters inside the word for check

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Keeping reserve soldiers under control.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to retain is to keep possession of, to go on holding something.

clue.text: Promises phosphorus-free new chemical compounds

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the remaining letters
free means without, so the letter for phosphorus is removed

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: Pledges of fresh chemicals without phosphorus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' removes P from PROMISES, leaving ROMISES, which 'new' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Isomers are compounds sharing a formula but differing in the arrangement of their atoms.

clue.text: Liaison of blonde chasing footballers from the East

indicators.note: chasing means following, so the word for blonde comes after
in an across clue, coming from the east means read right to left, backwards

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body
fair hair is blonde hair

explanation.surface: A blonde woman's fling with eastern footballers.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'from the East' means read right to left; FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a liaison is a secret romantic relationship, an affair.

clue.text: Scope of authority after turning clock back

indicators.note: back means in the opposite direction, so the clock word is read in reverse

parts.note: a timer is a clock, typically one turned or wound to set it running

explanation.surface: The extent of someone's powers after the clocks go back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' and 'back' together say the clock word is read backwards, borrowing the picture of clocks going back in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a remit is the area of responsibility given to a person or body.

clue.text: Church work must be duplicated quickly

indicators.note: duplicated means made twice, so the pair of pieces is repeated

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Church tasks have to be done twice over, and fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal idiom: chop-chop is a command to hurry up, meaning fast or promptly.

clue.text: Cool youngster docked and left

indicators.note: docked means cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a child is a youngster

explanation.surface: A cool kid gets shown the door and walks off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts CHILD to CHIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to chill is to cool, and chill as an adjective means cold.

clue.text: Turn game around and show backs to be contentious

indicators.note: around suggests letters spun about, so Turn and game are rearranged
backs here means goes backwards, so the musical's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Evita is a famous stage musical, a show

explanation.surface: Someone told to reverse a match and show their backs gets quarrelsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' is a noun, the stage musical Evita, which 'backs' sends backwards to ATIVE; 'around' scrambles the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an argumentative person likes to quarrel, as a contentious one does.

clue.text: Teaches Tom to wear polished suede

indicators.note: to wear something is to have it round you, so the cat goes inside
polished suggests the letters of suede are worked over and rearranged

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A tomcat dons smartly buffed suede.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' is not a name but a male cat; 'polished' scrambles the suede letters to EDUES, which wrap round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to educate someone is to teach or instruct them.

clue.text: Men without millions are inclined to sign up

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for millions is removed from Men

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million
a ship that lists leans to one side, is inclined

explanation.surface: Men short of money feel inclined to join up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes M from MEN, leaving EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to enlist is to join the armed forces, enrol or sign on.
